Policy on greeting routines in detail
The aim of this section is to explain why careful work counts

Greeting and intake routine

This section sets the standard for first contact at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. Staff must greet travelers in a steady, respectful manner and keep their attention on the animal, the carrier, and the booking record before moving to next steps. Calm behavior matters because pets read the room quickly, and a quiet desk helps prevent avoidable stress. Handlers must speak in clear plain language, avoid sudden gestures, and keep a safe distance until the animal is settled.

Every welcome should support safety first and speed second. If a traveler arrives with a pet that is restless, anxious, or difficult to secure, staff must slow the exchange and use humane methods only. Do not crowd the animal, raise your voice, or make fast movements that could unsettle it further. Offer practical guidance, confirm the travel documents that are needed, and direct the traveler to the correct holding area or service point without delay once the animal is stable. If a carrier appears damaged, poorly closed, or otherwise unsuitable, the desk must stop the handoff and arrange a corrected solution before the journey continues.

Routine desk work also includes steady record checks, careful handover notes, and prompt updates to the next team in line. When two travelers are waiting, staff should keep the order fair and the tone even. When a pet such as Otis is especially sensitive, the handler should use extra patience and reduce unnecessary contact. If a case is unusual, unclear, or outside normal practice, pause and ask the senior coordinator for direction rather than guessing. Simple, consistent conduct protects animals, supports travelers, and keeps the desk reliable.

For any issue that cannot be settled at the counter, contact the senior coordinator at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
